mainTopic: God's faithfulness at the sea, דרשות on הלל, and the nations' gifts to the משיח
overview: This amud finishes the story of גבריאל at the furnace of חנניה, מישאל ועזריה: when God keeps His old promise to him, גבריאל praises God with "ואמת ה׳ לעולם". רבי נתן says the fish of the sea said this verse instead. The background is that בני ישראל at ים סוף doubted the מצרים were dead. God made the sea give up the bodies and promised it one and a half times as many, with נחל קישון as guarantor. The promise was paid with סיסרא's 900 chariots, which the river swept into the sea, and the fish then praised God's truth. Next come short דרשות on פסוקים of הלל by ריש לקיש and רבא, about how כנסת ישראל stands before God. Then רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי sends רבי teachings from his father. They cover why the nations praise God, the gifts that מצרים and כוש will bring to the משיח, and why רומי's gift is rejected. The amud ends with רומי's huge stored wealth, which is destined for the תלמידי חכמים, and starts explaining the פסוק in ישעיהו that teaches this. רבי אלעזר's explanation of 'those who dwell before ה׳' continues on the next amud.

steps.title: גבריאל is sent down and praises God's truth
steps.stepSummary: גבריאל finishes his plan to cool the furnace from inside and burn it from outside. God tells him to go down. גבריאל then says "ואמת ה׳ לעולם".
steps.simpleTranslation: "…and I will burn from the outside, and I will make a miracle inside a miracle." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: "Go down!" At that moment גבריאל began and said: "And the truth of ה׳ is forever."
steps.whatsHappening: The story is ending: גבריאל offers a double miracle, God agrees, and גבריאל praises God's truthfulness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גבריאל's plan has two parts: cool the furnace inside to save the צדיקים, and burn outside to destroy the men who threw them in. That is the "miracle within a miracle." Earlier in the story, God promised גבריאל that he would save אברהם's descendants. When God says "Go down," that promise is fulfilled, so גבריאל praises God's truth.

keyTerms.meaning: and I will burn / set ablaze
the angel גבריאל, in charge of fire
"And the truth of ה׳ is forever" (תהלים קיז:ב)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of גבריאל's sentence. "I will burn from the outside" is still גבריאל talking, not God.

phrases.english: and I will burn from the outside,
phrases.notes: Burning the men who threw the צדיקים into the furnace

phrases.english: and I will make a miracle within a miracle.
phrases.notes: Cool inside and hot outside, at the same time

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: רֵד!
phrases.english: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Go down!
At that moment Gabriel began and said:
"And the truth of the Lord endures forever."
phrases.notes: God kept His old promise to גבריאל

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the גבריאל furnace story on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גבריאל said "ואמת ה׳ לעולם" when God fulfilled His promise to him.

steps.title: רבי נתן: the fish said this verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן gives a different view: the fish in the sea said "ואמת ה׳ לעולם". He bases this on רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: "And the truth of ה׳ is forever" was said by the fish in the sea, in line with what רב הונא said.
steps.whatsHappening: A different opinion is given about who said the verse. This step also sets up the next lines, which explain the reason using רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the verse was credited to גבריאל. רבי נתן credits it to the fish of the sea instead. The words "like רב הונא" tell us an explanation is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא who offers a different view
in line with what רב הונא said

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: "And the truth of the Lord endures forever" —
the fish in the sea said it,
in line with Rav Huna.
phrases.notes: Points ahead to the explanation

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different speaker for the same verse
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fish of the sea said "ואמת ה׳ לעולם".

steps.title: Israel lacked faith at the sea
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that generation was קטני אמנה, people of little faith. רבה בר מרי shows this from a פסוק: בני ישראל feared the מצרים were also coming up out of the sea alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב הונא said: the Jews of that generation were of little faith. This matches what רבה בר מרי taught: What does it mean, "They rebelled at the sea, at ים סוף"? It teaches that the Jews rebelled at that moment and said: "Just as we are coming up on one side, the מצרים are coming up on the other side."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the background for רבי נתן's view. בני ישראל doubted that the מצרים had really died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because בני ישראל lacked faith, they needed to see the dead מצרים with their own eyes. That need is what leads to the sea being told to throw out the bodies. רבה בר מרי reads "וימרו" (they rebelled) as describing exactly this doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who explains the פסוק

phrases.english: As Rav Huna said:
the Jews of that generation
were of little faith,
and as Rabba bar Mari expounded:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״וַיַּמְרוּ עַל יָם בְּיַם סוּף״ —
phrases.english: What is meant by "They rebelled at the sea, at the Red Sea"?
phrases.notes: תהלים קו:ז

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהִמְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה וְאָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: It teaches that the Jews rebelled at that time and said:
just as we are coming up on one side,
so the Egyptians are coming up on the other side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the background behind רבי נתן's view
steps.raayaObject: בני ישראל at the sea lacked faith
steps.raayaSupportSource: "וימרו על ים בים סוף" as explained by רבה בר מרי

steps.title: The sea objects and God promises one and a half
steps.stepSummary: God orders the angel of the sea to throw out the bodies. The sea argues that a gift should not be taken back. God promises one and a half times as many.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the angel of the sea: "Spit them out onto dry land!" It said before Him: "Master of the World, is there a servant whose master gives him a gift and then takes it back?" He said to it: "I will give you one and a half times their number."
steps.whatsHappening: God responds to Israel's doubt by telling the sea to throw the dead מצרים onto the shore. The sea complains that it is losing its gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drowned מצרים were a gift to the sea, meant as food for its fish. God promises a bigger gift later. פרעה had 600 chariots, and later סיסרא's 900 chariots drowned in נחל קישון, which is one and a half times as many.

keyTerms.meaning: the angel in charge of the sea
one and a half (times as many)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְשַׂר שֶׁל יָם:
phrases.english: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the angel of the sea:
Spit them out onto dry land!
It said before Him: Master of the World,

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ עֶבֶד שֶׁנּוֹתֵן לוֹ רַבּוֹ מַתָּנָה
phrases.english: is there a servant whose master gives him a gift
and then takes it back from him?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אֶתֵּן לָךְ אֶחָד וּמֶחֱצָה שֶׁבָּהֶן.
phrases.english: He said to it: I will give you one and a half times their number.
phrases.notes: Later fulfilled with סיסרא's army

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְשַׂר שֶׁל יָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: God's response to Israel's lack of faith
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God promises the sea one and a half times as many in return for giving up the מצרים.

steps.title: The Kishon as guarantor, and the bodies are thrown out
steps.stepSummary: The sea asks for a guarantee. God names נחל קישון as guarantor. The sea immediately throws out the bodies and Israel sees them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It said to Him: "Master of the World, can a servant sue his master?" He said to it: "נחל קישון will be My guarantor." Right away it spat them onto dry land, and the Jews came and saw them.
steps.whatsHappening: The sea wants a guarantee, since a servant cannot demand payment from his master. Once God names a guarantor, the sea gives up the bodies and Israel sees them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחל קישון is where סיסרא's army later drowned, so naming it as guarantor points to how the promise will be paid. When the promise came true, the fish praised God with "ואמת ה׳ לעולם", which explains רבי נתן's view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key to רבי נתן's view: God kept His promise to the sea, so its fish declared His truth.

phrases.english: It said to Him: Master of the World,
is there a servant who sues his master?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: נַחַל קִישׁוֹן יְהֵא לִי עָרֵב.
phrases.english: He said to it: The Kishon River will be My guarantor.
Immediately it spat them onto dry land
and the Jews came and saw them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the conversation between God and the sea
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With נחל קישון as guarantor, the sea threw out the מצרים and Israel saw them.

steps.title: Verse: Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק supports the story: Israel saw the מצרים dead on the seashore.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "And Israel saw the מצרים dead on the shore of the sea."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק as a source for the story it just told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says Israel saw the מצרים lying dead on the shore. That fits the story: the sea threw them out so that Israel's doubt would be answered.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on who said "ואמת ה׳ לעולם". One view is גבריאל, when he saved חנניה, מישאל ועזריה. The other is רבי נתן's view, the fish. They praised God when He kept His promise to give the sea a gift one and a half times as large, after it gave up the drowned מצרים.

phrases.english: As it is said:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת מִצְרַיִם מֵת עַל שְׂפַת הַיָּם״.
phrases.english: "And Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore."
phrases.notes: שמות יד:ל

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the story
steps.raayaObject: The sea threw the dead מצרים onto the shore where Israel saw them

steps.title: What was the 'one and a half times' payment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how God's promise of one and a half times as many bodies was kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'one and a half times their number' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about God's promise to the sea. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, God promised the sea one and a half times as many bodies as it was giving back. Now the גמרא wants to know which later event actually paid that amount.

keyTerms.meaning: One and a half (times as many)
Of them, compared to their number

phrases.english: What is the 'one and a half times' of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the promise made in Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which event fulfilled the 'one and a half times' promise, and how the numbers work out.

steps.title: Six hundred chariots versus nine hundred chariots
steps.stepSummary: פרעה had 600 chariots and סיסרא had 900, which is exactly one and a half times as many.
steps.simpleTranslation: About פרעה it says 'six hundred chosen chariots', and about סיסרא it says 'nine hundred iron chariots'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two פסוקים. One counts פרעה's chariots and the other counts סיסרא's chariots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 600 multiplied by one and a half equals 900. So the sea gave up פרעה's 600 chariots and was later paid back with סיסרא's 900. The rest of the story explains how those 900 ended up in the sea.

keyTerms.meaning: The Canaanite general defeated in the days of דבורה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the two armies. The 600 belong to פרעה at the sea, and the 900 belong to סיסרא many years later in the time of the שופטים.

phrases.english: For regarding Pharaoh it is written:
"Six hundred chosen chariots"
whereas regarding Sisera it is written:
"Nine hundred iron chariots"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The payment was סיסרא's 900 chariots, which is one and a half times פרעה's 600.

steps.title: The stars heat the iron and סיסרא's soldiers go into the river
steps.stepSummary: The stars fought סיסרא and made his iron spears burning hot, so his soldiers went down to cool off in נחל קישון.
steps.simpleTranslation: When סיסרא came, he attacked with iron spears. God took the stars out of their paths against them, as it says, 'From heaven the stars fought.' When the stars came down on them, the iron spears got hot. So the soldiers went down into נחל קישון to cool off and wash themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story of סיסרא's defeat. It explains how his army ended up in נחל קישון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'מן שמים נלחמו הכוכבים' is read literally: the stars came down and heated the iron weapons. This gets the soldiers into the river, which sets up the river's chance to pay its guarantee.

keyTerms.meaning: Their paths or orbits (of the stars)

phrases.english: When Sisera came,
he came upon them with iron spears;
the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought out against them
stars from their orbits, as it is written:
"From heaven the stars fought."
Since the stars of heaven came down upon them,
these iron spears became hot.

phrases.aramaic: נְחִיתוּ לְאַקְרוֹרֵי לְמִיסְחֵי נַפְשַׁיְיהוּ בְּנַחַל קִישׁוֹן,
phrases.english: They went down to cool off and bathe themselves in the Kishon River.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how סיסרא's 900 chariots, named in Step 8, came to the river.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stars heated סיסרא's iron weapons, driving his army into נחל קישון.

steps.title: נחל קישון pays its guarantee
steps.stepSummary: God tells נחל קישון to pay its guarantee, and the river sweeps the soldiers into the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: God said to נחל קישון: 'Go and pay your guarantee.' Right away נחל קישון swept them away and threw them into the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its high point: the guarantor named in Step 5 now pays the debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, the sea asked for a guarantor and God named נחל קישון. Now the river delivers the 900 chariots to the sea, so the promise is fully kept.

keyTerms.meaning: Your guarantee (what you promised as a guarantor)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְנַחַל קִישׁוֹן:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the Kishon River:
Go and pay your guarantee.
Immediately the Kishon River swept them away
and cast them into the sea,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְנַחַל קִישׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the soldiers now in the river, the river pays its debt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נחל קישון fulfills its role as guarantor by delivering סיסרא's army to the sea.

steps.title: The פסוק: the river swept them away
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק from שירת דבורה supports the story that נחל קישון swept them away.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'The river קישון swept them away, the ancient river.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to back up the story it just told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'נחל קישון גרפם' match the story directly. The unusual extra phrase 'נחל קדומים' will be explained next as a hint to the guarantee.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: as it is stated: "The Kishon River swept them away,
that ancient river"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That נחל קישון swept סיסרא's army into the sea.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שופטים ה:כא, 'נחל קישון גרפם נחל קדומים'.

steps.title: Why is it called the 'ancient river'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'נחל קדומים' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'ancient river' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about an unusual phrase in the פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling a river 'ancient' seems unnecessary. The גמרא expects this extra word to teach something.

phrases.english: What is "ancient river"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions a phrase in the פסוק from Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word קדומים.

steps.title: The river that became a guarantor long ago
steps.stepSummary: 'נחל קדומים' means the river that became a guarantor back at the time of יציאת מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the river that was made a guarantor long ago.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'ancient' hints at the guarantee the river took on at קריעת ים סוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדומים is connected to מקדם, 'from earlier times.' The פסוק is hinting that this river had an old debt from the days of פרעה, which it paid now. This ties the פסוק directly to the story.

phrases.english: The river that became a guarantor from long ago.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קדומים refers to the river's guarantee from the time of the sea.

steps.title: The fish praise God's faithfulness
steps.stepSummary: At that moment the fish of the sea said 'ואמת ה׳ לעולם', because God kept a promise made long ago.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that time the fish of the sea opened their mouths and said: 'And the truth of God is forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by showing why the fish said 'ואמת ה׳ לעולם'. This completes רבי נתן's view from Step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God kept a promise made centuries earlier, at the time of יציאת מצרים. That shows God's truth lasts 'forever'. So this line from הלל fits the fish, just as רבי נתן said.

keyTerms.meaning: And God's truth lasts forever (a line in הלל)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole story, from the doubt at the sea to סיסרא and נחל קישון, explains רבי נתן's view: the fish said 'ואמת ה׳ לעולם' because God kept a promise across many generations.

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה פָּתְחוּ דָּגִים שֶׁל יָם
phrases.english: At that time the fish of the sea began
and said: "And the truth of the Lord endures forever."

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה פָּתְחוּ דָּגִים שֶׁל יָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by returning to רבי נתן's claim.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The fish said 'ואמת ה׳ לעולם' when God's ancient promise to the sea was fulfilled through סיסרא's army.

steps.title: The Jewish people compare themselves to a rat in the house
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains 'מושיבי עקרת הבית': כנסת ישראל complains that her children treat her like a rat living in the corners of a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: What does the פסוק 'Who seats the barren woman of the house' mean? כנסת ישראל said to God: 'Master of the world, Your children have made me like this rat that lives in the hidden corners of houses.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new דרשה begins on a different פסוק of הלל. ריש לקיש starts explaining 'מושיבי עקרת הבית'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads עקרת הבית as linked to עיקרי בתים, the hidden lower parts of a house. Because of sin, כנסת ישראל feels pushed aside, like a rat with barely a place in the house. The פסוק's promise of being 'seated' and becoming a happy mother answers this complaint.

keyTerms.meaning: The barren woman of the house
The Jewish people as a whole
The hidden corners or foundations of houses

steps.confusionAlert: Here עקרת does not mean 'barren' in the simple sense. The דרשה reads it as related to עיקרי בתים, the hidden corners of a house.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
What is that which is written: "Who seats the barren woman of the house"?
The Congregation of Israel said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
Your children have made me like this rat
that lives in the vaults of houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, מַאי דִּכְתִיב: ״מוֹשִׁיבִי עֲקֶרֶת הַבַּיִת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the sea story and opens a new דרשה on another פסוק of הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'עקרת הבית' describes כנסת ישראל, pushed into the corners like a rat because of her children's sins.

steps.title: רבא: Israel is beloved when God hears her prayers
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains ״אהבתי כי ישמע ה׳״ as כנסת ישראל saying she knows she is loved when הקב״ה listens to her pleas.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the verse 'I love that God hears' mean? The Jewish people said: Master of the world, when do I know that You love me? When You hear the sound of my pleading.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a new explanation of a verse from הלל, reading it as the Jewish people speaking to God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the verse says 'I love God because He listens.' רבא reads it the other way: 'I am loved' is shown by the fact that God listens. Answered prayer is the sign of God's love.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jewish people as one whole, pictured as a single person
Master of the world, a way of addressing God
My pleas, my prayers for mercy

phrases.english: Rava taught: What is the meaning of what is written:
'I love that the Lord hears' (Psalms 116:1)?
The Congregation of Israel said:
Master of the Universe,
when am I beloved before You?
When You hear the voice of my pleas.
phrases.notes: Answered prayer is the proof of God's love.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new aggadic דרשה on another verse of הלל, after ריש לקיש's teaching in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כנסת ישראל knows she is loved by הקב״ה when He hears her prayers.

steps.title: רבא: Even when weak in מצוות, Israel belongs to God
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains ״דלותי ולי יהושיע״: although the Jewish people are poor in מצוות, they are God's, so it is fitting that He save them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I was brought low, and He will save me.' The Jewish people said to God: Master of the world, even though I am poor in מצוות, I am Yours, so it is fitting that I be saved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues with a second verse from the same chapter, again spoken by the Jewish people to God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״דלותי״ ('I was low') is read as being poor in מצוות. ״ולי יהושיע״ is read as 'it is fitting for me to be saved,' and the reason is 'I am Yours.' So the claim to be saved comes from belonging to God, not from earning it.

keyTerms.meaning: I was brought low, I became poor

steps.whatToRemember: Both of רבא's readings make the same point: God's bond with the Jewish people is love and belonging. It shows in answered prayer, and it holds even when they are weak in מצוות.

phrases.english: 'I was brought low, and He will save me' (Psalms 116:6).

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדַּלָּה אֲנִי בְּמִצְוֹת,
phrases.english: even though I am poor in מצוות,
I am Yours,
phrases.notes: The reason it is fitting: Israel belongs to God.

phrases.english: and it is fitting for me to be saved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second דרשה by רבא on the same chapter of תהלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when the Jewish people are lacking in מצוות, they belong to God, so it is fitting that He save them.

steps.title: רבי asks the sick רבי ישמעאל for his father's teachings
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא tells that when רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי was sick, רבי sent to ask him for two or three teachings he had said in the name of his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: When רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי was sick, רבי sent him a message: Tell us two or three things that you once told us in the name of your father.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. It opens a short story that brings in the next teachings, which come from רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי asks for these teachings while רבי ישמעאל is ill. The story itself teaches nothing yet. It frames the teachings from רבי יוסי that follow, through the message about רומי's wealth in step 32.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of your father

steps.confusionAlert: ״רבי״ here is a name, not a title. It means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
When Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei fell ill,
Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] sent to him:
Tell us two or three things
that you said to us in the name of your father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: כְּשֶׁחָלָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story that brings in a fresh set of teachings on הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story frame: רבי asks for רבי יוסי's teachings before they might be lost.

steps.title: Why should the nations praise God for His kindness to Israel?
steps.stepSummary: Quoting his father, רבי ישמעאל asks about ״הללו את ה׳ כל גוים״: what do the nations have to do with praising God for His kindness to us?
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back: This is what my father said. What does the verse 'Praise the Lord, all nations' mean? What business do the nations of the world have here?
steps.whatsHappening: The first teaching of רבי יוסי begins with a question on a verse from הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same psalm goes on to say 'for His kindness is great toward us.' So why are the nations told to praise God for kindness shown to Israel? The question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their business, what does it have to do with them?

phrases.english: He sent to him: So said my father:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'Praise the Lord, all nations' (Psalms 117:1)?
What do the nations of the world have to do with it?
phrases.notes: The next verse says 'for His kindness is great toward us,' meaning toward Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first answer to רבי's request from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the nations are told to praise God in a psalm about His kindness to Israel.

steps.title: The nations praise for their miracles, so all the more should we
steps.stepSummary: The nations praise God for the wonders He did for them. All the more so must Israel praise Him, since His kindness to us is so great.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: 'Praise the Lord, all nations' for the mighty acts and wonders He did with them. All the more so we, for 'His kindness is great toward us.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers his own question by reading the psalm as a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the psalm is about the nations praising God for what they experienced. The second half draws the lesson: if they praise Him, Israel must praise Him even more. The two halves of the psalm now fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying
All the more so (a קל וחומר)
His kindness is great toward us

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
'Praise the Lord, all nations'
for the mighty acts and wonders that He did with them;
phrases.notes: Sefaria translates this as 'before their eyes.'

phrases.english: all the more so we [must praise Him],
for 'His kindness is great toward us.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The nations praise God for their own miracles. By קל וחומר, Israel must praise Him all the more for His greater kindness to them.

steps.title: מצרים will bring a gift, and the משיח will want to refuse
steps.stepSummary: A second teaching of רבי יוסי: in the future מצרים will bring a gift to the משיח, and he will think he should not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another teaching: In the future מצרים will bring a gift to the משיח. He will think he should not accept it from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל sends a second teaching from his father. This step sets up a problem that God will solve in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משיח wants to refuse because מצרים enslaved and abused the Jewish people. This hesitation is the setup. God's reply comes next.

phrases.english: And furthermore:
In the future Egypt will bring a gift to the Messiah.
He will think he should not accept it from them.
phrases.notes: Because they enslaved Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: עֲתִידָה מִצְרַיִם שֶׁתָּבִיא דּוֹרוֹן לַמָּשִׁיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching sent in answer to רבי's request from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future מצרים will bring a gift to the משיח, who will at first hesitate to accept it.

steps.title: God says to accept, because מצרים hosted His children
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה tells the משיח to accept the gift, because מצרים once gave lodging to the Jewish people. At once the verse is fulfilled: ״יאתיו חשמנים מני מצרים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: God will say to the משיח: Accept it from them! They gave lodging to My children in מצרים. Immediately: 'Nobles shall come out of Egypt.'
steps.whatsHappening: God settles the משיח's doubt from step 21, and a verse from תהלים is shown to come true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though מצרים later enslaved Israel, they first gave the Jewish people a place to live, and that good is not forgotten. Once God approves, the gift is accepted. This fulfills the verse about nobles coming from מצרים.
steps.whatToRemember: Teaching on hosting: מצרים's early kindness in giving Israel a home is still rewarded in the days of the משיח, despite the slavery that followed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches the value of הכרת הטוב (gratitude). Even past kindness from an enemy is remembered and repaid.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַמָּשִׁיחַ:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, will say to the Messiah:
Accept it from them!
They gave lodging to My children in Egypt.
Immediately: 'Nobles shall come out of Egypt' (Psalms 68:32).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַמָּשִׁיחַ: קַבֵּל מֵהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the משיח's hesitation from step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משיח accepts מצרים's gift because they once hosted the Jewish people, fulfilling ״יאתיו חשמנים מני מצרים״.

steps.title: כוש reasons that its gift should also be accepted
steps.stepSummary: כוש makes a קל וחומר: if מצרים, who enslaved Israel, had its gift accepted, then surely כוש, who never enslaved them, deserves to have its gift accepted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: כוש will make a קל וחומר about itself: If these מצרים, who enslaved Israel, were treated this way, then I, who did not enslave them, surely should be!
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves on to the next nation. כוש sees that מצרים's gift was accepted, and it argues that its own gift should be accepted even more. This sets up הקב״ה's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning runs from 'weaker' to 'stronger.' מצרים had a big strike against it, because it enslaved Israel, and it was still accepted. כוש has no such strike, so by logic it deserves acceptance at least as much.

keyTerms.meaning: Made a 'how much more so' argument about itself
Is it not all the more so?

phrases.english: Kush will draw an a fortiori inference about itself:
phrases.notes: כוש sees that מצרים's gift was accepted.

phrases.english: If these (Egyptians), who enslaved them (Israel), are treated so,
phrases.notes: The 'weaker' case: מצרים was accepted even though it enslaved Israel.

phrases.english: then I, who did not enslave them,
all the more so (should be accepted)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds directly on step 22, where מצרים's gift was accepted. כוש uses that result as the base of its קל וחומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כוש argues that it deserves acceptance even more than מצרים, because it never enslaved Israel.

steps.title: God agrees and כוש's gift is accepted
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה tells the משיח to accept כוש's gift, and the פסוק 'כוש תריץ ידיו לאלהים' is fulfilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקב״ה will say to him (the משיח): Accept it from them. Immediately: 'Kush shall hasten to stretch out her hands to God.'
steps.whatsHappening: הקב״ה accepts כוש's argument, and the גמרא shows that this fulfills the second half of the same פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both halves of תהלים 68:32 have now come true. 'Envoys will come out of Egypt' matches מצרים's gift, and 'Kush shall hasten to stretch out her hands to God' matches כוש's gift. The קל וחומר worked.

keyTerms.meaning: Will hasten (to stretch out) its hands, offering a gift

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, will say to him (the Messiah):
Accept it from them.
Immediately: "Kush shall hasten to stretch out her hands to God" (Psalms 68:32).
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same verse quoted for Egypt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: קַבֵּל מֵהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers כוש's קל וחומר from step 23 by accepting it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: כוש's gift is accepted, and this fulfills תהלים 68:32.

steps.title: רומי reasons that its gift should also be accepted
steps.stepSummary: מלכות רומי הרשעה makes its own קל וחומר: if nations who are not Israel's brothers were accepted, then surely we, who are their brothers (through עשו), should be.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wicked kingdom of רומי will make a קל וחומר about itself: If these, who are not their brothers, were treated so, then we, who are their brothers, surely should be!
steps.whatsHappening: A third nation, רומי, steps forward and tries the same kind of argument. This sets up הקב״ה's very different reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רומי bases its claim on family ties instead of past behavior. As descendants of עשו (אדום), they are 'brothers' of יעקב's children. They argue that family should count for more than strangers like מצרים and כוש.

keyTerms.meaning: Their brothers. Rome descends from עֵשָׂו, יַעֲקֹב's brother
Edom, the nation of עֵשָׂו, which the Sages identify with Rome

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that רומי's argument works just because it has the same form as כוש's. The next step shows that הקב״ה rejects it completely.

phrases.english: The wicked kingdom (of Rome) will draw
phrases.notes: רומי is identified with אדום, the descendants of עשו.

phrases.english: an a fortiori inference about itself:
If these, who are not their brothers, are treated so,

phrases.aramaic: אָנוּ שֶׁאָנוּ אֲחֵיהֶן — לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?!
phrases.english: then we, who are their brothers, is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשְׂאָה מַלְכוּת (רוֹמִי) הָרְשָׁעָה קַל וָחוֹמֶר בְּעַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Copies כוש's successful argument from step 23, but replaces 'did not enslave' with 'we are brothers.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רומי claims that, as Israel's brothers, its gift deserves acceptance even more than the others'.

steps.title: God rejects רומי and orders גבריאל to rebuke it
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה tells גבריאל: 'גער חית קנה,' read as 'rebuke the beast, and acquire for yourself the congregation (of Israel).'
steps.simpleTranslation: הקב״ה will say to גבריאל: 'Rebuke the beast of the reed.' This means: rebuke the beast, and acquire for yourself the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: Rome's argument is turned down. Instead of accepting its gift, הקב״ה orders that Rome be rebuked, and He reads תהלים 68:31 as a wordplay to explain this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קנה is read as 'acquire,' and עדת (from later in the פסוק) is read as 'the congregation,' meaning Israel. Rome is the 'beast.' Its brotherhood does not help it, because it acted like a wild animal toward Israel. So it is rebuked, and Israel is taken back.

keyTerms.meaning: And acquire for yourself the congregation (Israel)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the turning point of the story. Unlike מצרים and כוש, רומי's קל וחומר fails, because its cruelty toward Israel outweighs any family connection.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְגַבְרִיאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, will say to Gabriel:
"Rebuke the beast of the reed" (Psalms 68:31) —
Rebuke the beast, and acquire for yourself the congregation.
phrases.notes: קנה is read as 'acquire,' and עדה refers to Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְגַבְרִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רומי's קל וחומר from step 25 by rejecting it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רומי's gift is not accepted. It is rebuked, and Israel is reclaimed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being Israel's 'brother' does not help a nation that behaved like a wild beast toward Israel.

steps.title: Second reading: the beast that lives among the reeds
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: 'חית קנה' is the beast that lives among the reeds, meaning the 'pig of the forest' from תהלים 80:14, which is a symbol of רומי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Rebuke the beast of the reed' means the beast that dwells among the reeds, as it is written: 'The boar from the forest ravages it, and the creatures of the field feed on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to read 'חית קנה.' Here קנה means real reeds, and the beast that lives there is identified using another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reading, קנה meant 'acquire.' Here it means 'reeds,' a swampy place where wild animals live. The proof פסוק describes a wild boar ravaging Israel's vineyard. The חזיר is a classic symbol for אדום/רומי, so the 'beast' is still Rome.

keyTerms.meaning: A pig (wild boar) from the forest, a symbol of רוֹמִי

phrases.english: Alternatively: "Rebuke the beast of the reed"
means the beast that dwells among the reeds,
as it is written: "The boar out of the forest ravages it,
phrases.notes: תהלים 80:14. The boar symbolizes אדום/רומי.

phrases.english: and the creatures of the field feed on it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same words, 'חית קנה,' that were explained in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'beast of the reed' is the wild boar of the forest, meaning רומי.

steps.title: Third reading: a beast whose deeds are all written with one quill
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads קנה as 'quill': rebuke the beast whose deeds are all written with one pen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Rebuke the beast whose deeds are all written with a single quill.
steps.whatsHappening: A third reading of 'חית קנה' is given. This time קנה means a writing reed, a quill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reed was used as a pen. Sefaria's English (based on Steinsaltz) explains 'all its deeds are written with one quill' as describing a nation that speaks of others in only one way, for the worse. Either way, it is once again Rome that is being rebuked.

keyTerms.meaning: An אָמוֹרָא who passes on teachings of רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Rebuke the beast
all of whose deeds are written with a single quill.
phrases.notes: קנה is read as a reed pen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third meaning of קנה ('quill'), alongside 'acquire' (step 26) and 'reeds' (step 27).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'beast of the reed' is a nation whose deeds are all written with one quill, meaning רומי.

steps.title: Rome slaughtered the mighty like ownerless calves
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the פסוק, 'עדת אבירים בעגלי עמים,' is explained: רומי slaughtered mighty people like calves that have no owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The congregation of mighty ones with the calves of the nations' means that they slaughtered mighty people like calves that have no owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of the same פסוק, showing another reason רומי deserves rebuke: it killed great people with no regard for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבירים ('mighty ones') refers to great and important people. Rome killed them as carelessly as someone would slaughter a stray calf that nobody owns and nobody will protect. This cruelty is the reason Rome's 'brotherhood' argument fails.
steps.whatToRemember: מצרים and כוש have their gifts accepted, each by a קל וחומר. רומי tries the same move, claiming to be Israel's brother, and is rejected. Every reading of 'גער חית קנה' points to Rome as a cruel beast that killed even great people as if they were ownerless calves.

phrases.english: "The multitude of the mighty, with the calves of the peoples" (Psalms 68:31) —
meaning that they slaughtered mighty people like calves
that have no owners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining תהלים 68:31, moving from 'חית קנה' to the next words, 'עדת אבירים.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רומי slaughtered great people like ownerless calves, which is why it is rebuked rather than accepted.

steps.title: The officials of רומי take money but do not serve their masters
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'מתרפס ברצי כסף' is explained: the Romans reach out to take money, but they do not do what their masters want.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Submitting himself with pieces of silver' means they stretch out a hand to receive money, but they do not do the will of the owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues explaining the same פסוק from תהלים (68:31) about רומי, now covering the words 'מתרפס ברצי כסף'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רצי is read as if it came from רצון, meaning 'will.' The point is that the Romans are greedy and untrustworthy: they eagerly take money, yet even after being paid they do not carry out the wishes of the people who pay them.

keyTerms.meaning: pieces of silver, here hinting at רָצוֹן (will)
the will of the owners or masters

phrases.english: "Submitting himself with pieces of silver" means:
that they stretch out a hand to receive money,
phrases.notes: Bribes or payments taken by the officials of רומי.

phrases.english: but they do not do the will of the owners.
phrases.notes: Wordplay: רצי read as רצון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the phrase-by-phrase reading of the same תהלים פסוק begun in steps 26-29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רומי takes money but cannot be relied on to do what it is paid for.

steps.title: Israel was scattered because it wanted closeness with the nations
steps.stepSummary: 'פיזר עמים קרבות יחפצון' is read to mean that Israel was exiled because it wanted closeness with the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He scattered the peoples who delight in war.' What caused Israel to be scattered among the nations of the world? The closeness with them that they desired.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last part of the פסוק and uses it to give a reason for Israel's exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קרבות (wars) is read as קריבות (closeness). The verse now teaches that Israel was scattered among the nations because Israel itself wanted to be close to them and copy their ways.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'peoples' in the פסוק as the nations being scattered. In this דרשה the ones scattered are ישראל, and the cause is their own desire to be close to the nations.

phrases.english: "He scattered the peoples who delight in war":
what caused Israel
to be scattered among the nations of the world?
The closeness with them that they desired.
phrases.notes: Wordplay: קרבות (wars) read as קריבות (closeness).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel's exile was caused by its own desire to be close to the nations.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole תהלים פסוק (68:31) has now been read as a description of רומי. Its last words explain that Israel's exile came from wanting closeness with the nations.

steps.title: The enormous food stores of the city of רומי
steps.stepSummary: Another message describes רומי's wealth: 365 markets, each with 365 towers, each with 365 floors, and each floor holding enough food for the whole world.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he further sent to him: There are 365 markets in the great city of רומי. Each one has 365 towers, each tower has 365 floors, and each floor holds enough to feed the entire world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, who has been answering רבי's request from step 18, sends him another message. This one describes the huge riches stored in רומי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number 365 is repeated at every level to show how vast רומי's wealth is: markets, towers, floors, each with enough food for the world. This description sets up the question in the next step: who is all this wealth really for?

phrases.english: And he further sent to him:
Three hundred sixty-five markets
are in the great city of Rome,
and each and every one has in it
phrases.notes: Text correction: (היו) replaced by [יש].

phrases.english: three hundred sixty-five towers,
and each and every tower has in it
three hundred sixty-five floors,
and each and every floor has in it

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לָזוּן אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ.
phrases.english: enough to feed the entire world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new message from the same sender, moving from the reading of the פסוק to a description of רומי's wealth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רומי's stored wealth is beyond measure.

steps.title: For whom is all this wealth stored?
steps.stepSummary: A sage asks רבי who all of רומי's stored wealth is meant for.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון ברבי said to רבי (and some say it was רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי who said it to רבי): For whom are all these?
steps.whatsHappening: After hearing about רומי's huge food stores, a sage asks a question. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes that so much wealth must serve some purpose in ה׳'s plan. The גמרא records two opinions about who asked it.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (an alternate version of who said it)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi said to Rabbi,
phrases.notes: Text correction: (ישמעאל) replaced by [שמעון ברבי].

phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Yishmael bar Yosei who said to Rabbi:
For whom are these?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the wealth described in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the intended beneficiary of רומי's vast stored wealth?

steps.title: The wealth is for the Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the wealth is for you, your colleagues, and their students, as the פסוק in ישעיהו says that the merchandise of the nations will go to those who dwell before ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: For you, for your colleagues, and for your colleagues' students, as it is said: 'Her merchandise and her hire shall be holy to ה׳. It shall not be stored and it shall not be hoarded, for it shall be for those who dwell before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that the wealth is ultimately meant for the Torah scholars, and a פסוק is brought as a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (ישעיהו 23:18) speaks of a wealthy nation whose gains will become holy to ה׳ and go to 'those who dwell before ה׳.' These are understood as the תלמידי חכמים. So רומי's riches are in the end destined for the people of Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section explains this פסוק phrase by phrase, so this step lays the foundation for what comes next.

phrases.english: For you, for your colleague, and for your colleagues' circle,
as it is said: "Her merchandise and her hire shall be holy to the Lord;
it shall not be stored and shall not be hoarded;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לַיּוֹשְׁבִים לִפְנֵי ה׳ יִהְיֶה וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: for it shall be for those who dwell before the Lord, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 23:18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wealth is destined for the תלמידי חכמים, based on ישעיהו 23:18.

steps.title: What does 'it shall not be stored' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the words 'לא יאצר' in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'it shall not be stored'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the פסוק it just quoted, starting with the phrase 'לא יאצר'. This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two similar-sounding phrases, 'לא יאצר' and 'לא יחסן'. The גמרא wants to know what each one adds.

phrases.english: What is "it shall not be stored"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the פסוק quoted in step 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'לא יאצר'.

steps.title: A storehouse and a treasury
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that 'לא יאצר' refers to a storehouse and 'לא יחסן' refers to a treasury.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: 'It shall not be stored' means a storehouse. 'It shall not be hoarded' means a treasury.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains the two phrases, showing that each one refers to a different kind of storage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית אוצר is an ordinary storehouse for goods like grain. A בית גניזה is a guarded treasury for valuables. The פסוק is saying that this wealth will not stay locked up in either kind of place, because it will be passed on to the righteous.

keyTerms.meaning: treasury, a hidden place for valuables

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
"It shall not be stored": this is a storehouse;
"and shall not be hoarded": this is a treasury.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לא יאצר means a storehouse; לא יחסן means a treasury.

steps.title: Who are 'those who dwell before ה׳'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'for those who dwell before ה׳' means, and introduces רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'for those who dwell before ה׳‎'? רבי אלעזר said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the פסוק and introduces רבי אלעזר, whose answer continues in the next part of the daf. This is a setup line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is who exactly counts as 'dwelling before ה׳.' Only the attribution to רבי אלעזר appears here; his actual explanation comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: What is "for those who dwell before the Lord"?
Rabbi Elazar said:
phrases.notes: His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the פסוק of step 34, moving to its next phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who are 'those who dwell before ה׳'?
